about.what: The English Prayer Rope Anthem is a contemporary Orthodox chant for the prayer rope, sung knot by knot as the rope is told. Verse by verse it lifts the rope's short prayers: to the Holy Trinity, to the Lord Jesus, to the Most Holy Theotokos, to St John the Baptist, and to all the saints and holy angels, each closing on the same refrain.
about.history: A devotional song of our own time, not a hymn of the Church's services. No author or composer is recorded for it, and no first recording: it passed from one Orthodox listener to another, and it is sung in several languages. Its verses are built on prayers said on the prayer rope: the Jesus Prayer, “Lord Jesus Christ, have mercy on me”, and the short prayers that many say on the rope as well, to the Holy Trinity, to the Theotokos, to St John the Baptist, to all the saints and to the angels.
about.when: Outside the services, at any hour. It belongs to no service of the Church, so it is not sung at the Liturgy, Vespers, Matins or the Hours. It is a song for prayer at home and on the way, and its words are those of someone praying with the prayer rope.

variants.label: English

lines.text: I will hold my prayer rope till I rise up to the sky,
the prayer is so short, but strong and can defy.
As I say the prayer more, my enemy will lose the war.
The prayer I say at first you will hear in every place:
Most Holy Trinity, save us all by Thy grace.
As I say the prayer more, my enemy will lose the war.
I will say out loud again the second prayer that will be:
Lord Jesus Christ, have mercy on me.
As I say the prayer more, my enemy will lose the war.
Third prayer I say out loud is to the Mother of our God:
Most Holy Theotokos, save us all.
As I say the prayer more, my enemy will lose the war.
Fourth to thee, Saint John, I pray, to wash all my sins away:
Baptizer of Christ, intercede for us all.
As I say the prayer more, my enemy will lose the war.
Fifth I pray to all the saints, who struggled hard with no complaints:
All Saints of God, intercede for us all.
As I say the prayer more, my enemy will lose the war.
At the end I pray to thee, O holy angels I don't see:
Archangels of God, intercede for us all.
As I say the prayer more, my enemy will lose the war.
I will hold my prayer rope till I rise up to the sky,
the prayer is so short, but strong and can defy.
As I say the prayer more, my enemy will lose the war.

variants.wordsSource: Taken down from the recording. No printed text of the anthem is known.

variants.label: العربية

lines.text: قد أمسكت المسبحة كي يرفع عني دعائي
lines.translit: Qad amsaktu l-misbaha kay yurfa'a 'anni du'a'i

lines.text: بقوة الصلاة أرتقي بين السماء،
بتكرارها الكثير سوف أغلب الشرير.
هذه أولى الصلاة تسمعونها في الحين
lines.translit: Hadhihi ula s-salati tasma'unaha fi l-hin

lines.text: أيها الثالوث القدوس خلّصنا أجمعين،
بتكرارها الكثير سوف أغلب الشرير.
الصلاة الثانية سأتلوها صادحًا:
ربي يسوع المسيح يا ابن الله ارحمني،
lines.translit: Rabbi Yasu' al-Masih ya bna llah irhamni,

lines.text: بتكرارها الكثير سوف أغلب الشرير.
الصلاة الثالثة لوالدة الإله،
أيتها الفائقة القداسة خلّصينا،
بتكرارها الكثير سوف أغلب الشرير.
الصلاة الرابعة ليوحنا المعمدان،
يا صابغ المسيح تشفّع لعبيدك،
بتكرارها الكثير سوف أغلب الشرير.
الصلاة الخامسة لجميع القديسين،
يا قديسي الله تشفّعوا بنا،
بتكرارها الكثير سوف أغلب الشرير.
وختامًا صلاة للملائكة،
يا رؤساء الأجناد تشفّعوا بنا،
بتكرارها الكثير سوف أغلب الشرير.

variants.wordsSource: An automatic transcription of the recording, set out in the song's own lines, as the English and French are; no printed text of the anthem is known. On the owner's word of 2026-10-31 it was checked against the singing, line by line and in pairs of lines, by an Arabic speech model and on the voice's own picture: the refrain (bi-takrariha l-kathir, sawfa aghlibu sh-shirrir) and lines 4, 5, 7, 8, 11, 19 and 20 are heard as written, line 4 ending fi l-hin (not fi kulli hin), and line 2 ending artaqi bayna s-sama'; line 14 is sung ya sabigha l-Masih, not ayyuha, and now reads so. Heard only in part, and marked unsure here until a listener who knows Arabic confirms them: the first word of line 1 (qad), the first words of line 2 (bi-quwwati s-salati), and lines 10, 13, 16 and 17. The transliteration is ours, as the words are sung. Each line is timed to the singing.
